newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia parliament flexes muscles on NATO, Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russia parliament flexes muscles on NATO, Chechnya.

text.p: The Russian parliament, flexing its muscles during President Boris Yeltsin's illness, issued strong protests on Friday against NATO's plans for eastward expansion and the peace process in rebel Chechnya.

The rhetoric by the State Duma lower chamber contrasted with statements by the government, which has toned down its criticism of both the defence alliance and domestic efforts to end fighting in Chechnya.
Its stand was likely to have few long-term consequences because Yeltsin removed most of the Duma's powers after a revolt by hardliners in 1993.

But it was a sign of the increased political tensions since Yeltsin, who has scarcely appeared in the Kremlin after his re-election in July, announced on September 5 that he would undergo heart surgery.
The Duma, where communists and their nationalist allies have a majority, said expanding NATO to take in Russia's former Warsaw Pact allies might recreate the tensions of the Cold War.

"A competition is developing between candidates for NATO membership whose consequences are hard to predict," said a statement which the Duma voted overwhelmingly to send to the United Nations and other international organisations.
"Problems of national minorities, unregulated inter-state arguments and claims against current borders could ignite the situation," it added.
The Duma also protested against what it called the takeover of Russia's Chechnya region by the separatist rebels, who signed a peace deal with ousted security chief Alexander Lebed in August.

Before his sacking, government officials had criticised Lebed for giving too much away to the separatists, but the government has since quietly ignored moves by the rebels to take power and split Chechnya from Moscow.
